speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, and weight loss, along with an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node. To help narrow down the cause, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea, constipation, or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any other swollen lymph nodes in your neck, armpits, or groin, and do you experience pain in the enlarged supraclavicular node when you drink alcohol? I also need to know if you have had any recent fevers or unexplained itching.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of smoking, or have you noticed any persistent cough or shortness of breath? REQUEST TEST: CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis.

text: The CT scan reveals massively enlarged lymph nodes in multiple regions, which strongly suggests a systemic lymphoproliferative disorder. To confirm the specific type of malignancy and guide treatment, I need tissue for pathological examination. REQUEST TEST: Excisional biopsy of the supraclavicular lymph node.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index indicates a B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. To further sub-classify the lymphoma and guide specific therapy, I need to assess the expression of other markers. REQUEST TEST: Immunohistochemistry for CD10, BCL6, and BCL2.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal immunohistochemistry results for CD10, BCL6, and BCL2 suggest this is likely a diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) rather than a germinal center subtype. I will now review the final pathology report to confirm the diagnosis and stage the disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL)
